title: Connector hub reads for its CLI
description: The control pair a connector uses to read the hub for the CLI on its own machine (C-05.26a, amendment A-05.3; 06 C-06.26a): hub.request carries one of three contract 10 read requests whole ({type, params}; 10 C-10.14 for ListMachines and ListChats, C-10.14a for GetChatAttach) and hub.response carries contract 10's answer whole ({ok, type, request_id, result} or {ok, type, request_id, error}), paired by re (C-05.10). The hub judges the request as the user who paired the machine (C-05.3 paired_by) and answers exactly as it would answer that user on POST /hub/api/read, the attach.read Activity entry included (10 C-10.14a). The body is contract 10's: schemas/10-hub-request.json, as its amendments replace it (A-10.1 for GetChatAttach), is normative for params and result, and this file closes the frame around it. The response body is the one 05 body that names a command text, an offered folder's real path or a chat in its cht_ id form (C-05.49, C-05.15 and section 2's chat label definition as A-05.3 amends them; 03 section 2 as A-03.3 amends it): it is data the machine's own user asked for, which the connector hands to the CLI and runs nothing from.

hub_request.description: One contract 10 read the connector forwards for the CLI on its own machine (C-05.26a). Direction: connector to hub. The hub answers every one with exactly one hub.response whose re is this frame's id. Pause (C-05.27) does not withhold it.

ch.description: The channel this frame travels on (C-05.10).

kind.description: The frame kind within its channel.

id.description: This frame's id, unique per sender per connection. The hub.response names it in `re`.

seq.description: Per connection, per channel, per direction: 1 for the first frame, plus 1 for each next (C-05.11). Durable positions live in the bodies (contract 07 cursors, hub_msg_id, contract 06 rev), never here.

at.description: When the sender built the frame. Informative; never used for ordering or expiry.

type.description: The closed list of read types a connector may forward for its CLI (C-05.26a): ListMachines (10 C-10.14, a signed-in user) and ListChats (10 C-10.14, Read on each chat listed) and GetChatAttach (10 C-10.14a, amendment A-10.1). Any other value fails this schema, which C-05.10 refuses as a bad frame (fatal, A-05.1), so the connector forwards nothing else and refuses the CLI itself (06 C-06.26a).

params.description: The type's params as contract 10 defines them (schemas/10-hub-request.json $defs/params_<type>; A-10.1's file for GetChatAttach); {} when it takes none. Contract 10's schema is normative for the body: the hub validates it as it validates a hub-API request, and a bad body comes back as 10's bad_request inside hub.response, never as a 05 error frame.

request.description: Contract 10's request body {type, params} (10 $defs/request), carried whole.

hub_response.description: The hub's answer to one hub.request (C-05.26a): contract 10's response body as the hub served it to the user who paired the machine (C-05.3 paired_by), result or error. Direction: hub to connector. The connector hands it to the CLI as received, caches nothing and runs nothing from it (C-05.15, C-05.49 and section 2's chat label definition as A-05.3 amends them; 06 C-06.26a).

ch.description: The channel this frame travels on (C-05.10).

kind.description: The frame kind within its channel.

id.description: This frame's id, unique per sender per connection.

seq.description: Per connection, per channel, per direction: 1 for the first frame, plus 1 for each next (C-05.11).

at.description: When the sender built the frame. Informative; never used for ordering or expiry.

re.description: The `id` of the hub.request this answers (C-05.10). Required: a hub.response is never unsolicited.

request_id.description: The id the hub minted for the read, 10's request_id (it is not the frame id).

result.description: The type's result as contract 10 defines it ($defs/result_<type>; A-10.1's result_GetChatAttach for GetChatAttach), served to the pairing user: for GetChatAttach the commands text and, for a folder chat, the offered folder's real path inside commands.shell and commands.code (06 C-06.14), and chats in 10's cht_ id form. Contract 10's schema is normative for it.

type.description: The request's type, echoed when the body named one.

request_id.description: The id the hub minted for the read, 10's request_id.

error.description: Contract 10's error (C-10.13) as served to the pairing user: not_found, forbidden with need, bad_request, rate_limited, unavailable.
